# CLIProxyAPI source-derived parity checklist for cliproxy-rs

Reference: `router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI`, branch `main`, commit **`6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2`**, committed `2026-10-02T11:00:47+08:00`. The requested `6fecc6e` resolves to this exact commit. All citations are immutable commit permalinks with repository-relative paths and line numbers. The source checkout is `reference/`. Research only; no Rust implementation and no upstream changes.

Every checkbox is one independently tracked inventory/contract item. Milestone counts include routes, translation registrations, configuration fields, ABI methods, and test-suite files; they are not estimates of engineering effort. An operation with multiple methods has one checkbox per method. Test-suite checkboxes cover all named tests in that file, not one checkbox per assertion. A feature can have separate runtime and configuration checkboxes. Milestones indicate the earliest required delivery phase, not isolation: later phases depend on earlier ones.

| Milestone | Scope |
|---|---|
| M1 | Claude OAuth, Anthropic Messages passthrough, model catalogs, client keys, native Claude fidelity |
| M2 | OpenAI Chat/Completions/Responses and Gemini/Interactions protocol conversion, including both directions with Claude |
| M3 | Codex, Antigravity, AI Studio, Vertex, Gemini keys, Kimi, xAI, Meta, Devin, OpenAI-compatible upstreams |
| M4 | Scheduler, cooldowns, retries, payload rules, aliases, proxies, shared config compatibility |
| M5 | Management API, WebSockets, realtime/live, operational access controls |
| M6 | Plugin ABI, TUI, discovery, Home control plane/cluster |

**Reading rules:** “stream” below means supported transport/handler behavior, not a guarantee that every model/provider supports that operation. Unsupported executor operations retain their native HTTP errors (often 501). OAuth credentials are open-ended flattened metadata objects, not closed structs. Sample values in `config.example.yaml` are not automatically runtime defaults. Rust serde defaults must follow loader defaults, normalization, and use-site fallbacks. Test inventories describe intended assertions from the actual test declarations; no Go tests or live upstream calls were executed for this research.

## 1. Public HTTP and WebSocket route inventory

Primary listener routes below are from `setupRoutes`. Ordinary `/v1`, `/openai/v1`, `/backend-api/codex`, and `/v1beta` groups use client authentication. Realtime uses separate standard/ephemeral credential middleware. OAuth callbacks, root, health, and panel routes are outside those groups. Management routes are catalogued separately in section 6.

## 2. Registered translator matrix and LOC

Direction is **inbound request format → upstream request format**. The registered response functions convert the upstream response back to that inbound format; they are not a separate forward response edge. Physical LOC includes blank/comment lines and `init.go`, excludes `_test.go` from implementation, and counts immediate `.go` files only. Shared helpers outside each pair directory are excluded. Where one directory registers several edges, its LOC is repeated, not apportioned or additive. Every `init.go` imported by `internal/translator/init.go` is included; there are no inferred edges.

Client IDs below are public OAuth application identifiers. Public source client-secret constants are deliberately not reproduced; compatibility must retain their source-defined values where the protocol requires them. ## 4. Scheduler, routing, retry, cooldown, and proxy semantics

- [ ] **[M4] M4-0018** Round-robin maintains previous selected identity per provider/model, not monotonically indexing shrinking candidate slices; deterministic fill-first; smooth weighted round-robin maintains signed running weights and route-model state keys. Exclude disabled/unavailable/nonmatching candidates before selection. [`sdk/cliproxy/auth/selector.go:1-1910`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/sdk/cliproxy/auth/selector.go#L1-L1910).
- [ ] **[M4] M4-0019** Highest available priority tier wins cold selection; priority default 0. Integer weight omitted=1, non-positive excludes only weighted selection, max 1,000,000; reject float/string/overflow YAML weights. Plugin scheduler across-priorities opt-in can receive all tiers. [`internal/credentialweight/weight.go:1-100`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/internal/credentialweight/weight.go#L1-L100).
- [ ] **[M4] M4-0020** Established session binding outranks recovered higher-priority credentials; fail over only when binding unusable. Session-affinity default false, TTL 1h, subagent inheritance default true; unbound requests use configured selector. Session aliases and routing aliases must not split execution/account identity. [`sdk/cliproxy/auth/session_cache.go:1-447`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/sdk/cliproxy/auth/session_cache.go#L1-L447).
- [ ] **[M4] M4-0021** Session identity precedence: explicit Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode/pi headers; prompt_cache_key; Responses conversation; legacy IDs; execution/derived identity; message hash fallback. Preserve parent/root/child relationships and cache cleanup. [`sdk/cliproxy/auth/session_resolver.go:1-53`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/sdk/cliproxy/auth/session_resolver.go#L1-L53).
- [ ] **[M4] M4-0022** Retry rounds: initial round 0 then request-retry additional rounds; each credential admitted only when effective nonnegative override >= round, negative/missing inherits global. max-retry-credentials caps distinct attempts per round; skipped credentials still age by round. Positive cooldown wait is capped by max-retry-interval, <=0 forbids waiting but not immediate failover/retry. Streaming bytes committed prevents replay; bootstrap retries apply only before commitment. [`sdk/cliproxy/auth/conductor_execution.go:1-2169`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/sdk/cliproxy/auth/conductor_execution.go#L1-L2169).

## 5. Configuration keys: canonical v8 paths, legacy paths, types, defaults, meanings

Each leaf below gives the Go type and source comment contract. `[]` marks a sequence element; `{provider}`, `{id}`, and `{key}` mark mapping keys. A struct is recursively expanded; free-form maps/JSON paths remain one leaf. Legacy aliases remain part of drop-in compatibility. Pointer defaults of nil mean inherit/use-site fallback, not false/zero. Zero-value defaults are before runtime fallback. A separate fallback inventory follows. Comment-only example values are illustrations, not assertions of defaults.
- [ ] **[M4] M4-0032** `client.codex.optimize-multi-agent-v2` (legacy `client.codex.optimize-multi-agent-v2`); type `bool`; default **false**. OptimizeMultiAgentV2 optimizes official Codex multi-agent requests across providers. Default false leaves the client's multi-agent behavior unchanged. [`internal/config/sdk_config.go:86`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/internal/config/sdk_config.go#L86).

EnableApplyPatch advertises freeform apply_patch only for supported models. Default false clears the capability regardless of template metadata. [`internal/config/sdk_config.go:90`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/internal/config/sdk_config.go#L90).

- [ ] **[M3] M3-0055** `multimedia.disable-image-generation` (legacy `disable-image-generation`); type `DisableImageGenerationMode`; default **false (DisableImageGenerationOff, integer enum 0 internally)**. DisableImageGeneration controls whether the built-in image_generation tool is injected/allowed.  Supported values: - false (default): image_generation is enabled everywhere (normal behavior). - true: image_generation is disabled everywhere. The server stops injecting it, removes it from request payloads, and returns 404 for /v1/images/generations and /v1/images/edits. - "chat": disable image_generation injection for all non-images endpoints (e.g. /v1/responses, /v1/chat/completions), while keeping /v1/images/generations and /v1/images/edits enabled and preserving image_generation there. - "passthrough": do not modify the tool list on non-images endpoints — keep image_generation if the client sent it and do not inject it otherwise; on /v1/images/generations and /v1/images/edits behave like "chat". [`internal/config/sdk_config.go:33`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/internal/config/sdk_config.go#L33).

GPTImage2BaseModel sets the base (mainline) model used by the legacy hosted image_generation tool path when a Codex image request is not proxied directly through the Image API.  The value must start with "gpt-" (case-insensitive). If empty or invalid, the default base model ("gpt-5.4-mini") is used. - [ ] **[M3] M3-0139** `oauth.providers.codex.stream-bootstrap-buffering` (legacy `codex.stream-bootstrap-buffering`); type `bool`; default **false**. StreamBootstrapBuffering holds back the frames that arrive before generation starts, none of which the client has seen anything from - the handshake (response.created, response.in_progress, the websocket metadata frames), keepalive heartbeats, and the *.added announcements of an item or part that is still empty - until the first generated event arrives. The upstream delivers server_is_overloaded rejections inside an HTTP 200 stream right after those frames instead of returning 503 on the wire, so buffering them keeps the downstream response headers uncommitted long enough to retry on another credential. Trade-off: the response headers are delayed until the upstream starts generating, which on a slow reasoning turn now means several heartbeat intervals rather than one, and can trip client or reverse-proxy read timeouts. The hold is bounded by a frame and a byte budget, not by wall-clock time, and neither budget is advanced by a websocket peer that sends only control frames or by an upstream that never terminates an SSE line. Only overload and rate-limit rejections fail over deliberately. A stream that ends while the bootstrap is still holding ends the attempt rather than reaching the client, and what follows is pre-existing but now far more likely, since the hold can span the whole reasoning phase instead of ending at the first keepalive: a clean end with no terminal event is request-scoped on SSE and stops there, while a websocket close or a transport error on either transport is not, so the request may be retried on another credential. Default is false. [`internal/config/config_types.go:203`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/internal/config/config_types.go#L203).
- [ ] **[M3] M3-0140** `oauth.providers.codex.stream-bootstrap-timeout` (legacy `codex.stream-bootstrap-timeout`); type `string`; default **empty/invalid → 0 (unlimited)**. StreamBootstrapTimeout specifies an optional maximum duration to hold back uncommitted response headers during bootstrap buffering before releasing the stream to the client. Defaults to "0" (unlimited time, relying purely on the 48-frame and 1MB byte bounds). FingerprintProfile selects the Claude Code request fingerprint for this credential on Anthropic Messages. Empty/default keeps the caller request fingerprint and headers, including first-party api.anthropic.com API keys. "claude-code-cli" opts official Anthropic API keys, custom gateways, and delegated providers such as Kimi into the Claude Code OAuth CLI Messages shape (OAuth betas, CCH signing, stable CLI identity) without treating the credential as a real OAuth token for refresh/profile/runtime semantics. CCH is a per-request hash and follows the native gate: it is emitted only on api.anthropic.com and Vertex, so an opt-in on any other gateway sends the billing block unsigned and cannot bust that gateway's prompt cache. Kimi strips the attribution entirely by default and keeps it, unsigned, after an explicit opt-in. count_tokens keeps the native model/messages/tools shape. Recognized values are defined by NormalizeClaudeFingerprintProfile. Arbitrary mapping keys are not additional fixed config fields: custom header names (for example X-Custom-Header), payload paths (for example service_tier), model/provider IDs, and plugin-owned config1/config2/config3/config-list/config-object are represented by their containing map/JSON leaf. Runtime-only Home and request bookkeeping fields tagged yaml:"-" are intentionally not YAML keys.

xAI/Meta key/model config types alias CodexKey/CodexModel, so the accepted YAML shape includes inherited fields; inherited source comments mentioning Codex do not imply a Codex upstream or Alpha Search support for those providers. Alias definitions [`internal/config/config_types.go:733-743`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/internal/config/config_types.go#L733-L743); provider-aware synthesis [`internal/watcher/synthesizer/config.go:246-264`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/internal/watcher/synthesizer/config.go#L246-L264).
- [ ] **[M6] M6-0045** Runtime-only Home schema is not an accepted top-level home config.yaml block because Config.Home is yaml:"-". HomeConfig nevertheless defines enabled bool=false, host string=empty, port int=0, disable-cluster-discovery bool=false, tls object; HomeTLSConfig defines enable bool=false, server-name string=empty, insecure-skip-verify bool=false, ca-cert string=empty. JWT bootstrap fills mTLS settings; node/client-cert/client-key/target-server-name fields are runtime-only. Home-received CPA HTTP port defaults to 8317 when nonpositive via NormalizeHomePort (distinct from normal loader port=0). [`internal/config/home.go:1-31`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/internal/config/home.go#L1-L31); [`internal/config/config.go:23-24`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/internal/config/config.go#L23-L24).

## 6. Management API route inventory and documentation reconciliation

Both versions are lazily registered once a management secret is configured, use availability + management middleware, and are disabled in Home mode. OAuth callback GET/POST skips management-key middleware but validates pending provider/state. Ordinary management endpoints use Bearer or X-Management-Key, local/remote policy and bcrypt validation. API route inventory here expands the four-method config wildcard loop explicitly. Bodies are operation-specific; source handler links include authoritative validation/output logic.

## 8. Golden-fixture and behavioral test suites worth porting

The following is a source-complete test-file inventory in compatibility-bearing packages, excluding benchmarks-only files. Each entry lists actual Test/Fuzz declarations with line anchors; the declaration names identify the assertion families. For a Rust fixture, lift the input and independently asserted expected bytes/JSON/headers/state, not a call to the Go converter as the expected value. Port streaming cases as ordered event/chunk sequences; fake clocks and transport mocks for scheduler/refresh; test native ABI/RESP/HTTP integration separately from pure goldens. Some tests require network fixtures/services and are integration contracts, not directly portable JSON fixtures.

### First fixtures to extract

These rows summarize existing suite checkboxes below; they do not add to milestone totals.

## 9. Ten highest-risk Rust-port contracts

1. **[M1] Native Claude TLS and ordered HTTP wire shape.** A normal Rust HTTP/TLS client can produce valid HTTP yet fail fingerprint parity. Match Node/OpenSSL ClientHello, ALPN, session resumption, exact header casing/order and proxy transports. [`internal/runtime/executor/helps/utls_client.go:1-430`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/internal/runtime/executor/helps/utls_client.go#L1-L430).
2. **[M1] Claude cloak, CCH, identity, beta and MCP remapping.** Stable credential identity and prompt-cache-sensitive signing interact with native detection, strict prompts, unknown betas, tools, thinking signatures and stream inverse mapping. [`internal/runtime/executor/claude_fingerprint_policy.go:1-141`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/internal/runtime/executor/claude_fingerprint_policy.go#L1-L141).
3. **[M2] Stateful streaming translators and signed reasoning.** One-to-many event conversion, partial tool JSON, indices, terminal events, encrypted/signed replay and provider cache-token accounting are easy to lose with serde roundtrips. [`sdk/translator/registry.go:1-442`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/sdk/translator/registry.go#L1-L442).
4. **[M4] Presence-preserving YAML migration and defaults.** Explicit false/zero/null/empty overrides, per-key inheritance, legacy/v8 precedence, comments and rejected-write nonmutation cannot be modeled by plain defaulted structs. [`internal/config/config_v8.go:1-792`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/internal/config/config_v8.go#L1-L792).
5. **[M4] Retry and cooldown state machine.** Request-scoped vs model/credential faults, retries per round, monotonic sibling deadlines, quota hints, cancellation and pre/post-commit streams must remain separate. [`sdk/cliproxy/auth/conductor_cooldown.go:1-2346`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/sdk/cliproxy/auth/conductor_cooldown.go#L1-L2346).
6. **[M5] Codex pooled/full-duplex WebSockets.** Response lineage/input deltas, one socket/account/model lifetime, liveness, bootstrap rejections, pinning and reconnect cannot be reduced to a stateless HTTP adapter. [`internal/runtime/executor/codex_websockets_duplex.go:1-599`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/internal/runtime/executor/codex_websockets_duplex.go#L1-L599).
7. **[M4] OAuth refresh concurrency and persistence.** Rotating refresh tokens, singleflight, auth-file watcher feedback, disabled/deleted file protection, per-request proxy and backoff can corrupt auth state if reordered. [`sdk/cliproxy/auth/conductor_refresh.go:1-842`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/sdk/cliproxy/auth/conductor_refresh.go#L1-L842).
8. **[M6] Home ambiguous-dispatch fencing and leases.** A post-send failure might already have issued a lease. Retrying can leak/duplicate active work; preserve fencing, release batching, revisions, cancellation and cluster failover. [`internal/home/client.go:1-2096`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/internal/home/client.go#L1-L2096).
9. **[M6] Native plugin ABI/RPC compatibility.** C calling conventions/memory ownership, platform loaders, schema negotiation and host callbacks/stream handles must interoperate with existing Go-built plugins. [`sdk/pluginabi/types.go:1-165`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/sdk/pluginabi/types.go#L1-L165).
10. **[M5] Realtime SDP/WebRTC and credential pinning.** ICE/TURN/private-IP limits, sideband/SIP state, ephemeral secrets and media lifetime create a much broader contract than /responses WebSockets. [`internal/client/codex/live/live.go:1-844`](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/blob/6fecc6e5567912661654a4eaf9b8f5436facd1c2/internal/client/codex/live/live.go#L1-L844).

These risk summaries reference existing checklist items and do not add to milestone totals.
